stories.title: Nvidia Halts Sales to Southeast Asia as U.S. Tightens China Restrictions
stories.summary: Nvidia has stopped selling to four countries in Southeast Asia. This action follows a new U.S. regulation that mandates licenses for companies in these nations to acquire advanced A.I. chips, indicating a tightening of restrictions related to China.

stories.title: US authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites for AI data centers in space
stories.summary: The U.S. has given authorization to SpaceX to launch one million satellites. These satellites are intended to support AI data centers in space.

stories.title: Big Trouble For Mark Zuckerberg? Meta's AI Smart Glasses Face Possible Ban In This Country Over Privacy Concerns
stories.summary: Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses are facing potential sales prohibition in the Netherlands. Consumer advocacy and digital privacy organizations are working to stop their distribution due to privacy concerns.

stories.title: BharatGen Patram 1.5 Explained: How India's New AI Model Reads Complex Documents And Images
stories.summary: BharatGen has introduced Patram 1.5, a new AI model with 7 billion parameters. This model is designed to interpret complex documents, images, and handwriting, extract information, and process files using natural language commands.

stories.title: IT sector employees seek national AI layoff policy as automation threatens jobs; unions and experts want
stories.summary: Employees in the IT sector are advocating for a national policy regarding AI-related layoffs. Unions and experts are also expressing their desire for such a policy as automation poses a threat to jobs.

stories.title: Trump Rejoiced in the Market’s Nvidia Surge. It Didn’t Last Long.
stories.summary: The stock market's recent decline indicates that the former president's efforts to reinstate a company's chief executive have faced challenges due to his other policies. This situation highlights a conflict between his stated desires and the actual economic environment.

stories.title: RBI Brings 60 Tonnes Of Gold Back To India, 84% Of Reserves Now Held Domestically
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has moved 60 tonnes of gold into its domestic vaults. This action means that 84% of India's gold reserves are now held within the country.

stories.title: US targeting India's manufacturing schemes while protecting its own industry: GTRI
stories.summary: The United States is examining India's manufacturing programs, such as the Production Linked Incentive scheme, and considering tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods due to concerns about excess manufacturing capacity. India asserts it does not have structural excess capacity and is in discussions for a trade agreement, while these potential tariffs are said to target multiple economies.

stories.title: NSE Becomes World's 3rd Largest Stock Exchange By Market Cap, Surpasses London Stock Exchange
stories.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has become the third largest stock exchange globally based on market capitalization. It has surpassed both the London Stock Exchange and Deutsche Boerse, reaching a market capitalization of $64.1 billion.

stories.title: Bulls back in charge, Sensex jumps 1.5k points, hits 84k mark
stories.summary: Indian stock markets saw a significant surge, with the Sensex climbing 1,500 points and reaching the 84,000 mark. This rise was driven by strong buying from both foreign and domestic institutional investors, along with declining crude oil prices and a strengthening rupee.

stories.title: 'Are we your servants?' Congress MP Imran Masood continues tirade against ally SP over seat-sharing
stories.summary: A Congress MP, Imran Masood, has reportedly continued to criticize his ally, the SP, regarding disagreements over seat-sharing arrangements.

stories.title: 'More obstructionist than opposition': PM Modi accuses Congress of weakening democracy on Constitution Da
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi has accused the Congress party of weakening democracy, describing them as more obstructionist than an opposition, during Constitution Day.

stories.title: Trump Floats Pardon for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Donald Trump has reportedly suggested the possibility of pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

stories.title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
stories.summary: Despite bipartisan interest in regulating artificial intelligence, efforts in Congress face challenges. The slow legislative process and disputes over jurisdiction could hinder the development of AI policy.

stories.title: US panel backs Dalai Lama’s succession Trust, as India gives it a Delhi base
stories.summary: A US panel has supported the Dalai Lama’s succession trust, which has now established a base in Delhi, India.

stories.title: IBM gives H-1B, green card holders 3 weeks to relocate from US or leave company; December 31 deadline set
stories.summary: IBM has given employees who hold H-1B visas and green cards three weeks to relocate from the US or face termination. The deadline for this decision is set for December 31.

stories.title: US green card process may get tougher for Indian workers as Labor Department releases revised PERM form a
stories.summary: The US Department of Labor has released a revised PERM form, which may make the green card process more challenging for Indian workers. This change could impact how foreign workers obtain permanent residency in the United States.

stories.title: H-1B visa delays leave skilled workers stranded abroad, says US Congressman
stories.summary: A US Congressman has stated that delays in H-1B visa processing are causing skilled workers to be stuck outside the country. These delays are affecting individuals who are seeking to work in the United States.

stories.title: Texas governor Hinojosa plans to lift H-1B visa freeze for state agencies
stories.summary: Texas Governor Hinojosa intends to remove the current freeze on H-1B visas for state agencies. This action would allow state agencies to once again sponsor H-1B visas for foreign workers.

stories.title: US student visa rule struck down: Relief for Indians, but what next?
stories.summary: A US student visa rule has been overturned, providing some relief for Indian students. The future implications of this decision are yet to be fully understood.
